name: Puerto Rico
summary: Puerto Rico has forced heirship: under the 2020 Civil Code half the estate is reserved for forced heirs, and the surviving spouse is now one of them. The other half is free. Puerto Rico has its own Trust Act (2012). The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force for the United States.
reserved_share: Forced heirs hold the legítima of 1/2 of the estate (down from 2/3), the free portion is 1/2 (Civil Code 2020, Law 55-2020, arts. 1621 and 1623). The surviving spouse is a forced heir in the first order with descendants (art. 1720). Individual fractions were not read.
foreign_law_note: No source read states how Puerto Rico's Civil Code 2020 treats the estate of a foreign national or whether the national law may be chosen.
trust_note: HCCH shows the United States as signatory only, with no extension. Puerto Rico Trust Act (Law 219-2012) creates a registered trust as a separate estate; Act 153 of 30 July 2026 amends it (adds revocable trusts). No private-foundation statute was found, only non-profit entities.
open_questions: Effective date and content of Act 153 of 2026 not read.
Whether forced heirship reaches trust assets was not checked.
Fractions per heir under the 2020 Code not read.
